title: Stress Detection Using Context-Aware Sensor Fusion From Wearable Devices
source_quotation:
[Dataset §V-A] "The dataset contains data for a total of 15 subjects"; the chest sensors are "ACC, ECG, RESP, EMG, EDA, TEMP" and the wrist sensors are "ACC BVP, EDA, TEMP". The classes are "(i) baseline (neutral), (ii) amusement, and (iii) stress"; for the 2-class problem, "baseline and amusement are grouped together in the non-stress class". [Methods §V-B.1] the signals are "segmented by a window of 60 seconds of data with a sliding length of 5 seconds". [Methods §V-B.3] the wrist branches use "Random Forest (RF)" and the chest branches use "the AdaBoost classifier"; "All classifiers are trained using leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation." [Results §V-D] the method achieves "86.34%" wrist 3-class accuracy and "94.12%" wrist 2-class accuracy, and achieves "86.19%" chest 3-class and "93.68%" chest 2-class accuracy.
[Dataset §V-A] "The dataset contains data for a total of 15 subjects"; the chest sensors are "ACC, ECG, RESP, EMG, EDA, TEMP" and the wrist sensors are "ACC BVP, EDA, TEMP". source_quotation:
[Methods §IV-A] "data were collected from 17 subjects; each took part in a 2-hour section. Unfortunately, due to device malfunction, data from subject 1 and 12 were discarded"; the study used "raw data obtained from the chest-worn ECG signal" and the WESAD tasks were "three affective states (Amusement, Baseline, Stress) and binary classification (Stress, No-stress)". [Methods §III-A] the method generates spectrograms from "one-second (1s) ECG segments" for the "vision transformer".
